note.note:
History:
- Presenting complaint: 3 days of profuse, watery diarrhea (6–7 stools/day) with intermittent crampy lower abdominal pain localized to the left side.
- Associated symptoms/timing: Vomiting at symptom onset (stopped currently). Felt feverish at symptom onset but no measured temperature documented; currently denies ongoing fever. Weakness/shakiness and reduced appetite. Able to tolerate fluids (soups, smoothies). Symptoms impairing daily activities and work; patient continued to go to work.
- Exposure: Ate a Chinese takeaway ~4 days ago. One child in household had vomiting (no diarrhea).
- Course/progression: Symptoms began ~3 days ago and have persisted; vomiting resolved early, diarrhea continues.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma; uses an inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- No other chronic illnesses reported.
- Allergies: Not documented / none reported.
- Medications: Inhaler only (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Social: Lives with wife and two children. Works as an accountant. Non-smoker, does not drink alcohol.

Physical Examination:
- No formal physical exam findings recorded; clinician planned conservative management and did not document vitals or exam.
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Relevant positives/negatives from history: 
  - No blood in stool.
  - No blood in vomit.
  - Vomiting has stopped.
  - Currently tolerating oral fluids.
  - Patient reported feeling feverish at onset but no measured temperature.
- Mental status / general exam: Not recorded.

Impression:
- Most likely: Acute infectious gastroenteritis, viral etiology favored (likely viral "stomach bug") causing watery diarrhea with initial vomiting.
- DDx-consistent alternatives:
  - Bacterial foodborne gastroenteritis (possible given recent Chinese takeaway) — medium likelihood; incubation period and crampy pain compatible.
  - Acute sigmoid diverticulitis — lower likelihood but considered because of localized left-sided pain (DDx lists as less likely). 
- No conflict noted between transcript and DDx.

Management Plan:
- Conservative outpatient management advised:
  - Oral rehydration and continued fluid intake; use oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) as available.
  - Paracetamol for symptomatic relief of fever/aches: advised "two tablets up to four times a day" (as stated by clinician).
  - No antibiotics recommended at this stage.
  - Recommend rest and time off work: advised 2–3 days off to allow recovery.
- Safety net / follow-up:
  - Return/reassess if symptoms do not improve in 3–4 days.
  - If ongoing symptoms, clinician may obtain stool sample and consider further investigations.
- Immediate tests/procedures: None ordered at this visit.

Patient Summary:
- Patient with 3 days of watery diarrhea (6–7/day), intermittent left lower abdominal cramp, initial vomiting (now resolved), and transient feverish feeling after eating a takeaway ~4 days ago. Most likely diagnosis is acute infectious gastroenteritis (viral most likely; bacterial foodborne illness also possible). Plan: oral rehydration, symptomatic paracetamol, rest, and outpatient follow-up if not improving in 3–4 days.

Key Takeaways:
- Keep well hydrated; use oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) as needed.
- Take paracetamol for fever/aches per advice (two tablets up to four times daily as stated).
- Rest and take 2–3 days off work; return for review if no improvement within 3–4 days.

Next Steps:
- No immediate investigations; arrange stool testing only if symptoms persist or worsen.
- Review/clinic follow-up if no clinical improvement in 3–4 days or sooner if new concerning features develop.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: documented vital signs (temperature, pulse, BP, respiratory rate), focused abdominal physical examination findings, allergy status clearly documented, inhaler dose/regimen not specified, medication reconciliation.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted; DDx entries are consistent with transcript.
- Transcript quality: Clear and complete; minimal inaudible/noisy sections.
